lead.headline: Russia frees jailed American teacher as Witkoff meets Putin
lead.dek: Stephen Hubbard, held since 2022 on mercenary charges, was at a St. Petersburg airport, Putin said
body: Russia freed Stephen Hubbard, a retired Michigan schoolteacher jailed on mercenary charges, as U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff met President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Wednesday, Witkoff and Russian state media said. Putin told Witkoff that Hubbard was at the city's Pulkovo airport, the TASS news agency reported.

Hubbard was detained in Ukraine in 2022 and sentenced after a closed trial in 2024 to nearly seven years in prison. Prosecutors said he signed a contract with the Ukrainian military; he denied it, and the State Department designated him wrongfully detained. President Donald Trump said Tuesday he had pressed Putin on the case: "I've asked him to release him."

The meeting followed talks Tuesday in Oslo between Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that a U.S. official said produced "meaningful progress." Witkoff is to carry Ukrainian and European proposals to Putin, who still demands all of Ukraine's Donetsk region. ABC News, citing U.S. officials, reported a deal to free more jailed Americans was near but not final.

briefs.headline: Musk says SpaceX and Tesla boards weigh a merger
briefs.summary: Elon Musk said Tuesday special committees of both boards are studying a combination he called uncertain; it would be the largest corporate tie-up on record.

briefs.headline: Alabama governor spares Toforest Johnson from execution
briefs.summary: Gov. Kay Ivey commuted Johnson's death sentence to life without parole Tuesday, citing doubts about the evidence in a deputy's 1995 killing. She said it was not a finding of innocence.

briefs.headline: Nor'easter closes Highway 12, empties Hatteras of visitors
briefs.summary: Overwash shut N.C. Highway 12 and Dare County kept a mandatory evacuation order for Hatteras Island visitors Tuesday as gusts to 50 mph and 6- to 12-foot waves hit the coast up to New Jersey.

briefs.headline: Kagan says court majority has weakened democracy
briefs.summary: Justice Elena Kagan said Tuesday at Catholic University that rulings on gerrymandering, voting rights and campaign money have undermined democracy.

briefs.headline: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case in Abuja
briefs.summary: A woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive in Abuja, Nigeria's Health Ministry said Tuesday. Minister Muhammad Pate said 44 contacts are being traced.

briefs.headline: North Korea orders border troops to act if South threatens
briefs.summary: State media said troops should take "prompt and resolute action" if South Korean forces threaten them, a day after Seoul vowed to punish further provocations.

briefs.headline: Houthis claim missile strike on coalition camp in Aden
briefs.summary: Spokesman Yahya Saree said the group hit a Saudi-led coalition operations room at Badr Camp. A police official told Al Jazeera smoke rose near Aden's airport.

briefs.headline: Lula dares Bolsonaro to open bank and phone records
briefs.summary: Lula said he would release his family's bank, tax and phone records if Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro did the same, five days before Sunday's presidential runoff.

briefs.headline: Morrisey lets dyed diesel on roads under 60-day emergency
briefs.summary: The order suspends penalties for highway use of red-dyed diesel in all 55 counties, about 20.5 cents a gallon less, with AAA putting diesel at $6.34.

briefs.headline: Boone jury grants mercy to grandmother in starvation death
briefs.summary: Jurors recommended parole eligibility after 15 years for Donna Stone, 79, convicted in Kyneddi Miller's 2024 death; sentencing is set for Dec. 8.

briefs.headline: WV public school enrollment falls by 8,270 students
briefs.summary: Certified count of 226,687 is down 3.5% from last year, with every county losing students in the first year of universal Hope Scholarship eligibility.

briefs.headline: Mason levy renewal tied to $90M a year in data center taxes
briefs.summary: Treasurer Larry Pack's report says the Monarch and Tamarack sites could yield $90.3M a year for schools only if voters renew the excess levy Nov. 3.

regional.item: Huntington leaders announced a $1 million plan Tuesday to bring a Thomas Dambo troll to the Huntington Museum of Art's grounds in 2027.
Six people have died this year in two crashes at the I-64/I-77 split, and WVDOT plans high-friction surfacing there as soon as next week.
Wood County nears a three-year deal to pay Camden Clark Ambulance about $850,000 a year, half the $1.7 million first sought, with no new tax.

away.item: Three Bennington-area fire departments were named Unsung Heroes at the October Walloomsac Walk, the Banner reported Tuesday.

hotspots.item: The Webster County Commission meets at 9 this morning in Webster Springs, its first session back on a twice-monthly schedule, the Echo said last week.
Surf City named retired Highway Patrol first sergeant Jason Casteen police chief Tuesday; Chief William Nas, hired in August, leaves Nov. 6 for Florida.

briefs.headline: Severed fibre line knocks out Rogers internet across the north
briefs.summary: Rogers blamed third-party construction crews for a Tuesday cut that hit Prince George, Quesnel, Fort St. John and Dawson Creek; rural repairs could take 24 to 48 hours.

briefs.headline: Councillor-elect flags $895M facilities bill for new council
briefs.summary: Bob Radloff said the 20-year civic facilities plan could mean a 30% tax increase; the new council is seated next month with the civic core plan deferred to it.

briefs.headline: Conservatives hold 5-point lead as B.C. advance voting closes
briefs.summary: Innovative Research's Oct. 15-19 survey of 1,153 adults found under 10% undecided; pollster Greg Lyle called the Eby-Doerkson leadership race a statistical tie.

briefs.headline: Alberta immigration questions pass as Smith vows reforms
briefs.summary: With about 90% counted, yes led eight of nine referendum questions, 54% to 58% on immigration; only opting out of federal programs trailed. Smith takes questions at 11:30 a.m. MT.

briefs.headline: 33 soldiers still in hospital as Wainwright holds vigil
briefs.summary: Defence Minister David McGuinty gave the figure Tuesday in Ottawa; the military had counted 39 injured, 19 critically. The town's first public vigil is Wednesday night.

briefs.headline: Phone-free classes lifted grades in Indian trial
briefs.summary: Students scored higher when phones were boxed at the start of each lesson, a trial of 16,683 students in India found, published Tuesday in Science.

briefs.headline: Marsquake points to active faulting in Valles Marineris
briefs.summary: A 2021 marsquake recorded by NASA's InSight lander points to a fault still slipping 20 to 40 kilometers beneath the Martian canyon, a study in Nature Communications found.

briefs.headline: Under-skin implant lets two patients steer prosthetics
briefs.summary: Phantom Neuro said two patients in Melbourne received a forearm implant that reads muscle signals, in an early feasibility trial of the device.

briefs.headline: Umbrella review finds no firm autism link for Tylenol
briefs.summary: Seven meta-analyses covering more than 3 million people showed associations that disappeared when only high-quality data were examined, the authors wrote this week.

briefs.headline: Anthropic drafts bill to halt high-risk AI releases
briefs.summary: The company's draft would let the Commerce Department ask a judge to block a model posing imminent risk of more than 50 deaths or $1 billion in damage.

briefs.headline: UK regulator asks firms to report AI near-misses
briefs.summary: The Financial Conduct Authority's Jessica Rusu said Monday that incident reporting should extend to significant AI failures and near-misses.

briefs.headline: Anthropic says Claude designed scorpion-toxin binders
briefs.summary: The company said its model generated 318,484 designs; of 211 tested in labs, 17 met binding criteria. Antivenom activity has not been tested.

weather_ear: Jim Claudtore's Wednesday forecast follows at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster and Summers-New River carry no regional line today; the Webster County Commission appears in Vacation Hotspots.
